due_when.clears_when: EITHER claude-pr-automerge.yml's branches filter is widened to cover lane/** (or whatever branch pattern lane dispatches actually use) and the NEXT lane-branch Tier-1 self-land PR is observed to auto-merge without a human click, OR the manager adopts a different, stated mechanism for landing lane-branch Tier-1 PRs and that mechanism is observed working once.

origin.rerun: mcp__github__actions_list list_workflow_runs, owner=benbaichmankass repo=metis-insights, resource_id=321655014 (claude-pr-automerge.yml), workflow_runs_filter.branch=<a lane/** branch with a green, declared-self-land PR open> -- expect total_count: 0 for as long as the branches filter excludes lane/**. Also: grep -n 'branches:' .github/workflows/claude-pr-automerge.yml to confirm the filter has not already been widened by someone else.

what: claude-pr-automerge.yml's push trigger is scoped to `branches: ["claude/**"]` (.github/workflows/claude-pr-automerge.yml:111), so a lane branch named per the manager's own dispatch convention -- `lane/<slug>` (e.g. `lane/perp-evidence-regen-3bps`, this session's branch) -- can NEVER trigger it, no matter how correctly the PR is declared (pr-landing self-land + arming file + merge-slot claim, all present and committed on that branch). OBSERVED, not inferred: PR #12937 sat green (mergeable_state clean, all 4 required checks success, check_pr_landing.py reports 'OK -- state=declared_self_land') for 20+ minutes with zero claude-pr-automerge runs against lane/perp-evidence-regen-3bps (mcp__github__actions_list list_workflow_runs for workflow_id 321655014, branch filter, returned total_count: 0; querying without the branch filter shows the workflow's last 10 runs are ALL on claude/tender-mayer-2g1vtq, the manager's own commit-to-main branch). So every Tier-1 self-land PR opened from a `lane/**` branch is stranded at 'ready, CI green' with no automated path to merge -- the exact 'seven of the night shift's PRs sat open, green and unlanded' failure mode .github/pr-landing/README.md was written to fix, reintroduced by a branch-naming convention (lane/**) that postdates the guard's claude/** assumption. Calling mcp__github__merge_pull_request directly to route around it is ALSO blocked -- not by the repo's own merge-slot guard (which this session satisfied: real committed claim at .github/merge-slots/lane-perp-evidence-regen-3bps.json) but by Claude Code's platform-level auto-mode classifier, which denied the guard's own prescribed workaround (touching the local /tmp marker file) with reason 'Merge Without Review' and explicit instructions not to pursue the same outcome through another tool. So a lane-branch Tier-1 self-land PR has no working path to merge at all today: not the intended relay (branch filter excludes it), not a direct merge call (platform classifier blocks it). Fix is either (a) widen claude-pr-automerge.yml's branches filter to also match lane/**, or (b) have the manager's spawn convention use claude/**-prefixed branch names for lanes that will self-land, or (c) an explicit operator/manager click-merge path for lane-branch Tier-1 PRs. Not this lane's call to make (workflow-file edit is landing machinery, R12: a PR changing the landing machinery may not land itself by it) -- filed for the manager/operator to decide. PR #12937 itself is unaffected by which fix is chosen; it just needs one human click-merge in the meantime, or an operator-approved workflow edit to unblock every future lane-branch PR at once.
